full_judgment:
3. The petitioner's case in short is, that he is a monthly tenant under the landlord-opposite party in respect of the suit premises and the opposite party filed the aforesaid two suits for ejectment of the petitioner on the ground of default in the payment of rent and also for bonafide requirement. It is the further case of the petitioner that when the landlord refused to accept the rent he started to deposit the rent with the House Rent Controller in House Rent Control Case Nos. 22 and 23 of 1987. Subsequently the House Rent Controller dismissed both the aforesaid cases against which the petitioner preferred Miscellaneous Appeal Nos. 215 of 1989 and 216 of 1989 before the District Judge, Dhaka. It is also the case of the petitioner that during the pendency of the aforesaid Miscellaneous Appeals the petitioner filed application under section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying further proceeding of the SCC Suits till disposal of the Appeals. The learned SCC Judge rejected the prayer and then the petitioner moved this Court and obtained Rules in Civil Revision Nos 781 and 782 of 1989 but those were subsequently dismissed for non-prosecution on 28.8.90. In the meantime the aforesaid appeals were dismissed by the learned District Judge against which the petitioner moved this Court and obtained Rules in Civil Revision Nos. 538 and 539 of 1990. The petitioner then filed these two applications praying for stay of the SCC Suits filed for ejectment. 

 4. Mr. M Gholam Rabbani, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the SCC Suits were filed for ejectment of the petitioner on the ground of default of payment of rent and also for bonafide requirement. He further submits that the House Rent Controller found that the petitioner is a defaulter and on such a finding he rejected the Rent Deposit cases against which the petitioner preferred the Miscellaneous Appeals which were dismissed and the petitioner moved this Court and obtained aforesaid two Rules. The learned Advocate submits that when the House Rent Controller has decided the point of default which was affirmed by the Appellate Court and if the suits for ejectment are allowed to proceed pending disposal of the two applications before this Court the petitioner will be highly prejudiced. 

 6. Admittedly both the suits were filed for ejectment of the petitioner who is a monthly tenant on the ground of default in payment of rent and also for bonafide requirement. It is also an admitted fact that earlier the petitioner moved the Trial Court for stay of further proceeding of both the suits. That prayer on being rejected the petitioner moved this Court in two Revisional applications which were dismissed for non-prosecution. After that during the pendency of these two revisional applications the petitioner has not moved the Trial Court afresh and prayed for stay of all further proceedings. The petitioner now filed these two applications before this Court and prayed for passing an order of stay of all further proceeding of the suits on the ground that there was decision on the point of default. In the House Rent Control case the only point at issue was whether the petitioner has deposited the rent in accordance with the provision of House Rent Control Ordinance. The House Rent Controller is not required to decide anything with regard to default in payment of rent. But he has dismissed the Miscellaneous Cases on the ground of default though as a matter of fact the ground for such dismissal has been non-compliance of the provision of House Rent Ordinance for such deposit. The Co below, that is the House Rent Controller, ought not to have made any specific observation to the effect that the petitioner is a defaulter in a case filed under section 19 of the House Rent Control Ordinance. The question whether the petitioner is defaulter or not is to be decided in the suit for ejectment and the finding of the House Rent Controller on the point of default will have no binding effect on the SCC Judge while deciding the suits on merit. That after consideration of the materials on record and after hearing the learned Advocates of both the sides I am of the view that the petitioner ought to have first moved the Trial Court for stay of further proceeding. At this moment there is no ground before me to stay all further proceeding of the SCC suits now pending before the Trial Court as the decision of the House Rent Controller and its subsequent affirmance by the Appellate Court on the ground of default will have no binding effect on the Trial Court.
